messages:
Nora (AE): Verdant POC: customer reports sporadic 429s and TTFT spikes after a warmup script. They ran batch=30 + prefetch across 25 clients. Can SE/SRE advise? :wave:
Evan (SE): Which model/runtime and are they in our VPC/private deployment? Any client logs showing kv lock timeouts?
Nora (AE): Model: atlas-8b (fp16), avg prompt 260 tokens, peaks 900. They're on our VPC Private deploy with restricted egress. Client logs show lines like "kv_lock_wait=1200ms" and gateway 429 responses around the same window.
Lin (ML): KV lock wait + large batch + long contexts = classic contention. Prefetching many different prefixes will expand shard working set and cause evictions and waits. Also check quantization path some fp4 kernels have higher tail latency for long contexts.
Maia (SRE): Infra metrics: tenant sustained high active requests at 2087654100; router ingress queues spiked and our per-tenant concurrency limiter returned 429s. VPC egress shaping also added backpressure for some of their external warmup traffic.
Evan (SE): Short-term fixes to recommend: 1) disable global client prefetch; 2) lower batch.max_requests to 8-12; 3) enable streaming so first byte arrives earlier; 4) stagger warmup with jittered starts. Example snippet to share:
```json
{"batch": {"max_requests": 12, "max_delay_ms": 8}, "prefetch": "staged", "stream": true}
```
Nora (AE): They asked if Dedicated with private tenancy would eliminate this and what the SLA/price delta looks like for a short trial.
Maia (SRE): Dedicated isolates cache and egress noise which helps, but it does not prevent bad warmup patterns. For POC we can provision a pre-warmed Dedicated node for a short trial; Sales Ops must quote. SLA wise, Dedicated gets higher uptime SLOs and dedicated performance targets compared to hosted.
BillingBot: quick-estimate: entry Dedicated pod (8xGPU class) ~ "$K/month" baseline; trial discounts may apply. For exact pricing contact Sales Ops.
Lin (ML): Also suggest using /v1/prefetch?mode=staged to serialize prefetch by shard, or implement client-side jitter. If first-token latency is critical, prepare a small prefix pre-cache list for their top prompts.
Evan (SE): Ask them to reproduce with the tuned client config and attach 3 traces (warmup, steady, spike) with X-Trace-Id or X-Request-ID. We need traces to see whether time was spent in gateway -> router -> runtime decode or waiting on KV locks.
Nora (AE): Action items: 1) I'll send the client snippet and ask them to run a phased warmup with jitter and collect 3 traces; 2) Maia will provision a temporary concurrency bump if they want to replay a controlled test; 3) I'll loop in Sales Ops for a Dedicated trial quote and SLA details.
Maia (SRE): I can bump per-tenant concurrency from 20 -> 36 for 2 hours and monitor eviction rate/queue depth. Will rollback if eviction rate rises too much. :white_check_mark:
Nora (AE): Thanks team. Ill update the customer and close unless they still see TTFT > 1s or more 429s. :raised_hands:
